records.rationale: The record contains only author and venue metadata, so it provides no substantive abstract evidence of an SE comparison or transferable mechanism.
MapCoder empirically evaluates four specialized agents spanning retrieval, planning, generation, and debugging across eight code benchmarks, providing direct primary SE multi-agent evidence.
ConTested shows that human-guided co-evolution of generated code and tests corrects unreliable majority voting with small measured overhead, providing a transferable agent assurance loop.
GiantRepair combines LLM patch skeletons with context-aware program analysis and realistic fault localization, providing a tested hybrid remedy for unreliable direct patch use.
Self-planning decomposes complex intent before implementation and improves correctness, readability, and robustness over direct and chain-of-thought code generation.
CodeT5+ supplies useful model and benchmark background for code generation but does not study agents, coordination, or a production assurance mechanism.
This citation-generation study evaluates document-grounded text answering rather than software development, and its mechanism is not demonstrated as an SDLC control.
Project-level domain adaptation materially improves generated unit-test coverage and mutation scores over CodeT5, A3Test, and GPT-4, offering a concrete complementary testing method.
HumanEval-X adds a concrete multilingual code benchmark and CodeGeeX supplies real-user productivity evidence, providing transferable evaluation support for coding-agent comparisons.
Self-Edit uses test execution feedback and a fault-aware editor to repair generated code, producing large accuracy gains across nine models and two benchmarks.
NGST2 couples neural search with concolic execution to prune invalid candidates and outperforms baselines in Java and Python modernization, providing a transferable hybrid verification pattern.
DreamCoder's learned component library and search policy are indirect program-synthesis background without LLM agents, SE-focused evaluation, or production controls.
RhoSynth turns developer changes and feedback into deployed static-analysis rules with measured precision, providing a production-tested verification and human-refinement mechanism.
This theoretical synthesis comparison explains the scalability-generality trade-off between deductive and enumerative methods but offers only indirect pre-LLM background.
TRANX constrains generated formal representations with target syntax and generalizes across evaluated code tasks, offering a transferable structural reliability control.
AutoPandas combines explicit API constraints with neural guidance on real-world synthesis tasks, providing an evaluated constrained-generation pattern for tool-using code agents.
The abstract claims improved neural-synthesis scale and precision but gives too little method or evaluation detail and no LLM-agent or transferable production evidence.
Keyword programming is historical Java code-assistance background but neither evaluates LLM agents nor supplies a production assurance mechanism.
This tutorial on proof-based deductive synthesis supplies foundational formal-correctness context but no LLM-agent evidence or empirical production test.
Interactive Synthesis enforces Java syntax, types, and scope while translating free-form developer intent and repairing expressions, providing a transferable constraint mechanism for code agents.
